NEW DELHI: Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami on Monday criticised Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge over his remarks concerning Prime Minister Narendra Modi 's father and targeted Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav over his alleged use of the term "infiltrators" for the people of Uttarakhand.Dhami questioned the Congress party's alliance with the Samajwadi Party, saying it must decide whether the alliance or the self-respect of Uttarakhand was more important to it.Reacting to Kharge's remarks, Dhami said, "Making such absurd and inappropriate remarks about the Prime Minister's father is entirely unbecoming in a democracy, and they have completely shattered all norms of decency."This comes after a person present at the Patna event on Sunday said that Prime Minister Narendra Modi would not go anywhere. Responding to the remark, Kharge said, "Modi ka baap bhi jayega."He also raised the issue of Akhilesh Yadav's reported remarks about the people of Uttarakhand, pointing to his political association with the Congress leadership."Meanwhile, Akhilesh Yadav, who is in an alliance with the Congress and is a close friend of Rahul Gandhi, has used the term infiltrators in reference to the people of Uttarakhand," Dhami said, criticising the language allegedly used by the Samajwadi Party chief.Dhami also referred to incidents of police firing during the Uttarakhand statehood movement, alleging that Akhilesh Yadav's father, during his tenure as chief minister, had ordered firing on statehood agitators. Referring to the incidents at Khatima, Mussoorie, Shriyantra Tapu and Rampur Tiraha, he said, "What else could we expect from him?"The Uttarakhand chief minister further pointed out that Akhilesh Yadav's wife hails from the state and said he should refrain from using such language about its people. "His own wife hails from Uttarakhand. He should, at the very least, refrain from using such language," Dhami said.Questioning the Congress party's political alliance with the Samajwadi Party, Dhami said the Congress leadership must clarify its priorities. "Furthermore, the Congress party is in an alliance with him; they must decide what they value more, this alliance or the self-respect of Uttarakhand," he said.The CM also inspected the newly constructed bridge and tunnel project in Rudraprayag, developed under the Char Dham road project.After reviewing the project details, the chief minister announced that it would be formally inaugurated soon. During his visit, he also toured the Sangam Library under the district administration's "Donate a Book, Plant a Tree of Knowledge" campaign.Constructed at an estimated cost of Rs 156 crore under the Char Dham road project, the infrastructure features a 200-meter-long bridge over the Alaknanda River and a 900.30-meter-long tunnel. Including the approach roads, the project spans a total length of approximately 1.18 kilometres and directly connects the Kedarnath National Highway (NH-107) with the Badrinath National Highway (NH-07).Vehicular movement on the bridge-tunnel route commenced on a trial basis on Monday. Once regular traffic begins following its formal inauguration, pilgrims travelling to the Kedarnath and Badrinath shrines will no longer need to pass through the congested Rudraprayag main market.This bypass will significantly reduce traffic pressure in the town during the Char Dham Yatra, bringing much-needed relief from traffic jams to both local residents and pilgrims.Emphasising that a smoother, safer, and well-organised Char Dham Yatra is a top priority for the state government, chief minister Dhami noted that improved road connectivity and modern infrastructure not only facilitate devotees but also boost local trade, tourism, and employment opportunities. Additionally, he reviewed ongoing slope stabilisation and protection works across landslide-prone zones along the Rudraprayag-Gaurikund National Highway, which aim to minimise landslide risks and make the pilgrimage route safer and more resilient.During his inspection of the Sangam Library, the chief minister lauded the innovative "Donate a Book, Plant a Tree of Knowledge" initiative spearheaded by District Magistrate Vishal Mishra. The campaign aims to cultivate an interest in reading among students, provide essential study materials for competitive examinations, and enrich local libraries.Receiving enthusiastic support from public representatives, officials, and citizens alike, the campaign has already gathered over 2,500 books for the Sangam Library, covering competitive exams, general knowledge, literature, and various other subjects. Contributing to the drive, chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami personally donated 150 books.Addressing the gathering, the chief minister remarked that books are a vital medium for acquiring knowledge and building personality. He highlighted that community-supported book donation drives are particularly beneficial for students in need of study materials for competitive exams and will foster a strong culture of reading and learning among the youth.District Magistrate Vishal Mishra stated that the books collected through the campaign are being made readily accessible to students and general readers, directly benefiting young aspirants preparing for competitive exams. He added that through active public participation, efforts are underway to transform local libraries into effective hubs of study and knowledge enrichment.chief minister Dhami earlier participated in the Shobha Yatra (procession) organised at the Municipal Corporation in Dehradun to mark the occasion of Maharishi Valmiki Prakatotsav. During the event, the chief minister announced that the honorarium for sanitation workers employed across various state departments would soon be increased, adding that a meeting would be convened shortly to finalise the decision.Paying rich tributes to Maharishi Valmiki on his birth anniversary, the chief minister stated that through the great epic Ramayana, Maharishi Valmiki introduced the entire world to the life and ideals of Lord Shri Ram. He noted that Maharishi Valmiki's life teaches us that a person can become an inspiration to others through noble thoughts and righteous deeds.Emphasising that an individual's true identity is defined by their knowledge, actions, and contribution to society, he added that Maharishi Valmiki inspired the creation of an egalitarian society free from discrimination.Highlighting the core teachings of the Ramayana, chief minister Dhami said the epic conveys timeless human values such as truth, righteousness (dharma), sacrifice, and duty. It guides humanity to walk the path of righteousness while upholding love, equality, fraternity, and human dignity.He remarked that the Ramayana teaches us that a person is judged not by their caste or social standing, but by their character, actions, and dedication. He further emphasised that Sanatan culture has always championed mutual respect, love, harmony, and social cohesion.The chief minister stated that under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, India is setting new benchmarks of development while preserving its rich cultural heritage. A new era of reconnecting with our roots, honouring our history, and strengthening cultural consciousness has begun. He pointed out that alongside the construction of the grand Shri Ram Temple in Ayodhya under the Prime Minister's leadership, dedicating spaces within the temple complex to Maharishi Valmiki, Nishadraj, and Mata Shabari stands as a testament to social harmony and inclusive cultural traditions.Noting that the international airport in Ayodhya has also been named after Maharishi Valmiki, the chief minister said that the central government is continuously integrating the poor, underprivileged, Scheduled Castes (SC), Scheduled Tribes (ST), and backward classes into the mainstream. Flagship initiatives such as the PM Awas Yojana, Ujjwala Yojana, Ayushman Bharat, Jal Jeevan Mission, and free ration distribution have empowered crores of families to lead better lives. Furthermore, legal provisions to protect the rights of SC and ST communities and prevent atrocities against them have been significantly strengthened.Reiterating Prime Minister Modi's vision that a developed and empowered nation can only be built by ensuring equal opportunities and dignity for all, chief minister Dhami stated that the Uttarakhand government is working tirelessly for the upliftment of marginalised and deprived sections.Concluding his address, the chief minister remarked that Uttarakhand is Devbhoomi-a sacred land enriched by the penance of sages, deep faith in holy shrines, and ancient traditions. The state government remains committed to strengthening cultural heritage alongside modern development, passing ancient values on to the younger generation, and providing equal opportunities for all. He expressed confidence that, guided by the ideals of Maharishi Valmiki, the state will successfully realise the vision of building a developed Uttarakhand.
Article Summary: Pushkar Singh Dhami criticises Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge over his remarks concerning Prime Minister Narendra Modi's father. He also criticises Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav over his alleged use of the term "infiltrators" for the people of Uttarakhand.

NEW DELHI: The BJP on Monday posted a striking message amid the political sparring ahead of the INDIA bloc’s November 1 rally in Delhi. It declared on its official X account, “Sorry to break it to you, all anti-Indian forces, BUT Modi kahi nahi jayega (Modi won't go anywhere)”.The post aimed to take a swipe at the opposition amid a row over Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge's remark, "Modi ka baap bhi jayega."Meanwhile, pressure on the Congress to postpone its rally to after Diwali has been growing as traders have raised concerns that closures will disrupt businesses.BJP's jibe comes ahead of Congress' "mega rally" at Ramlila Maidan, which the opposition plans to use to intensify its campaign against alleged irregularities in the SIR of electoral rolls and demand the resignation of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.The rally has also triggered protests from Delhi's traders, who fear that security arrangements, road closures and traffic diversions could disrupt business during the crucial festive season. Traders demonstrated at Kashmere Gate on Monday, urging the Congress to reschedule the event and allow markets to operate without disruption.During the protest, traders raised the slogan, "20,000 vaipariyo ki ik hi pukar, Diwali ke baad kijiye rally ka vichar (20,000 traders have one appeal: hold the rally after Diwali)".The Chamber of Trade and Industry (CTI) chairman, Brijesh Goyal, said the traders would write to leaders of all parties in the INDIA bloc, besides Congress president Kharge and Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi, asking them to defer the rally."We will write to leaders of all the parties in the INDIA bloc, urging them to hear our sentiments and postpone the rally," Goyal said.He expressed concern over the Congress's claim that around 10 lakh people could attend the rally, arguing that the gathering could severely affect wholesale markets around Ramlila Maidan."Business will be heavily impacted because, as reports suggest, 10 lakh people might gather at Ramlila Maidan, whereas its actual capacity is around 50,000," Goyal said.He cited a gathering at Jantar Mantar on October 10, claiming that the presence of around 2,000 to 4,000 people had led to metro station closures, barricading and restrictions. More than 20 major markets were forced to shut down, he alleged.According to Goyal, a rally of the anticipated scale could affect more than 20 wholesale hubs within a 5-km radius of Ramlila Maidan. These include Chandni Chowk, Sadar Bazar, Khari Baoli, Naya Bazar, Chawri Bazar, Daryaganj and Kashmere Gate.He said road closures could prevent three to four lakh buyers from outside Delhi, who visit the capital daily, from reaching the markets. Local customers could also stay away because of traffic restrictions.Rahul Gandhi, meanwhile, responded to the traders' concerns in a post on X on Monday, saying the protests would "stop in 30 seconds" if they asked Modi to sack chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the "vote chori" issue.Paramjeet Singh Pamma, president of the Sadar Bazar Bari Market Trade Association, also appealed to the Congress leadership to postpone the rally. He said the festive season was crucial for traders to recover their business across the year.Pamma warned that restrictions around major wholesale markets, including Sadar Bazar, Chandni Chowk, Khari Baoli, Fatehpuri and Azad Market, could cause losses worth crores of rupees, as traders and buyers from Delhi and other states flock to these areas during the festive season.The traders have urged the Congress to hold the rally after Diwali to avoid disrupting business during one of the busiest periods of the year.

MUMBAI: SBI has inaugurated CyRIS, a Cybersecurity Centre of Excellence, to strengthen cyber defence and threat intelligence across the financial sector. The centre was inaugurated by Department of Financial Services secretary Sanjay Lohiya in the presence of SBI chairman CS Setty and senior officials.CyRIS integrates cyber policy, training, research, innovation, threat intelligence and defence under three pillars: THINK, INNOVATE and DEFEND. THINK focuses on policy, talent development and public awareness; INNOVATE on research, new solutions and cybersecurity benchmarking; and DEFEND on threat detection, incident response and preparedness.Its focus areas include digital forensics, malware analysis, ethical hacking, fraud analytics, AI security and quantum-safe technologies. The centre will also foster collaboration among government and regulatory bodies, banks, fintechs, academia and technology partners.SBI chairman CS Setty said cybersecurity was central to customer trust and the digital financial ecosystem. “CyRIS will strengthen our ability to anticipate emerging threats and stay ahead of the evolving cyber landscape,” he said.Lohiya said cyber resilience needed to keep pace with financial digitisation.“CyRIS is a timely initiative to strengthen capabilities, collaboration, and preparedness across the ecosystem,” he said.SBI said it uses layered security controls, regular audits, vulnerability assessments, incident-response mechanisms, cyber drills and employee training to strengthen its defences. Nearly 1.81 lakh employees completed mandatory cybersecurity e-learning in FY26. The bank also runs customer-awareness initiatives on digital safety and fraud prevention.
Article Summary: CyRIS integrates cyber policy, training, research, innovation, threat intelligence and defence under three pillars: THINK, INNOVATE and DEFEND. Its focus areas include digital forensics, malware analysis, ethical hacking, fraud analytics, AI security and quantum-safe technologies.

Article Title: Watch: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay launches one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns
Article Text:
Vijay presented 22-carat, one-gram gold rings to 25 newborns. (PTI)

Who is eligible for the gold ring?

Scheme draws on Tamil tradition

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. He also held some of the newborns and presented the rings to beneficiaries during the launch programme.Under the scheme, eligible babies born in government hospitals and government primary health centres will receive a 22-carat, one-gram gold ring.The initiative, named the Maternal Uncle Gold Ring Scheme (Thaaimaman Thanga Mothiram Thittam), has an annual allocation of Rs 755.83 crore.It is aimed at celebrating motherhood, promoting maternal and child health and encouraging institutional deliveries by increasing public confidence in government healthcare facilities.The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions.Mothers must be registered under the Pregnancy and Infant Cohort Monitoring and Evaluation (PICME) system and have a Reproductive and Child Health (RCH) ID. They will also have to provide an e-KYC-verified Aadhaar card along with one of the prescribed identity or residence documents.These include ration cards, voter identity cards, Labour Welfare Board identity cards, Department of Posts address cards and nativity certificates.The state government has already procured 1.28 lakh one-gram gold rings for the initial rollout. Each ring will have a unique serial number and will be packed in tamper-proof packaging.From Monday, babies born in government hospitals will receive the rings at the time of discharge, according to the state government.To clear the backlog of eligible babies born between June 22 and Monday, the government will distribute the rings through 107 hubs across Tamil Nadu.Distribution will begin at the rate of 100 babies per day at each hub. At designated centres, 25 beneficiaries will be accommodated in the morning and another 25 in the afternoon to avoid overcrowding, PTI reported.Village Health Nurses will distribute invitations informing beneficiaries of their allotted date and time. Beneficiaries have been asked to visit the designated centres only at the time mentioned in their invitations.The district administration has also made transportation arrangements for beneficiaries from their respective areas. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election as a symbolic gift to newborns, drawing on the Tamil tradition of ‘Thaimaaman Seer’. The scheme has retrospective effect from June 22, Vijay’s birthday.A government order issued on June 23 described the initiative as a token celebrating the birth of a child, motherhood and the cultural tradition of ‘Thaimaaman’.According to ANI, Tamil Nadu minister Arun Raj explained the cultural significance of the initiative saying, "A maternal uncle is someone who is among the first to rush in when a child is born, sharing in his sister’s happiness as his own. He assures her that he will always stand by her and her child, offering love, support and a sense of security.""Today, the Tamil Nadu Government, under the leadership of our brother, Mr. Vijay, is embracing this sacred bond of the maternal uncle and, as a gesture of that affection, is set to provide a one-gram gold ring to every child born in government hospitals. When the scheme was announced and the question arose as to where it should be launched, the place chosen by our Chief Minister was Madurai. This is the sacred soil of Madurai, blessed with the compassion and grace of Mother Meenakshi," he added.Tamil Nadu records around 7.8 lakh deliveries annually, with institutional deliveries accounting for 99.9% of births, according to NFHS-6. Government health facilities account for nearly 4.2 lakh deliveries, or around 53% of the total.According to the state government, the average out-of-pocket expenditure for a delivery at a government hospital is Rs 1,364, compared with Rs 63,473 at a private hospital.The government said the scheme is intended to encourage safe institutional deliveries, strengthen maternal and child welfare and increase public trust in government healthcare services.The Tamil Nadu Medical Services Corporation will procure the gold rings based on annual requirements, while a project and programme management unit will oversee implementation and monitoring.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election.

Article Title: Delhi landfill garbage mountains shrinking, 100 acres reclaimed in 18 months: CM Rekha Gupta
Article Text:
Delhi CM Rekha Gupta poses for a group picture during an on-site inspection of waste disposal operations near Okhla, in New Delhi

Government targets legacy and fresh waste

New processing plants at three sites

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Poll Vote & Share your view What is your top concern regarding pollution in Delhi? Landfill waste Air quality Water quality (Yamuna) Dust pollution 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Focus on pollution and waste management

NEW DELHI: Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta on Saturday said the garbage mountains at the city's landfill sites were steadily shrinking as she reviewed waste disposal work at Okhla and laid the foundation stone for new waste processing facilities at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola.Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years, with a large portion of the cleared area also being turned green.She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed."Today, at Okhla, we have processed almost all the legacy waste that was there before January 2025," Gupta said.Gupta said the government was working on two fronts: clearing the existing garbage mountains while ensuring that fresh waste generated every day did not accumulate into new landfill sites.According to news agency ANI, she said around 3,000-4,000 metric tonnes of fresh waste reaches the sites daily and is being processed round the clock."The garbage currently piled up here is essentially fresh waste generated after January 2025, and that too is being processed round the clock. So, we are fighting on two fronts: one is eliminating waste, and the other is ensuring that the 3,000 to 4,000 metric tons of fresh waste arriving daily is processed immediately, so that new garbage mountains are not formed for future generations," Gupta said.She said the government was working to reduce the existing garbage mountains to zero."People are seeing that the garbage mountains are continuously shrinking and soon a time will come when they will become zero," Gupta said.Gupta also said she had taken what she described as her "last selfie" with the garbage mountain at Okhla."Today I have taken my last selfie with the garbage mountain; after this I have taken a pledge that this garbage mountain will end soon," she said.Taking a jibe at the Opposition, Gupta added, "I had said - garbage mountain, you will have to go; the opposition mocked. Today I will say the garbage mountain is going; now only its back remains."During the programme at the Okhla SLF site, Gupta laid the foundation stone for fresh waste processing plants at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola, as well as a biogas facility at Ghazipur. She also inaugurated the M&CW Centre at Kotla Mubarakpur through virtual mode from Okhla.The Okhla plant will be built at a cost of Rs 103 crore and will have a processing capacity of 1,400 metric tonnes per day.The Singhola facility will cost Rs 42 crore and have a capacity of 800 metric tonnes per day, while the Ghazipur plant will have a processing capacity of 700 metric tonnes per day.The facilities are intended to process fresh waste as well as construction and demolition waste. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure."Waste should not remain waste; Delhi should use it as wealth," she said, adding that new technologies were being introduced for waste segregation and processing.She said waste and cattle dung would be used to produce biogas and manure as part of efforts to build a technology-driven waste management system.Gupta said the government was taking up several measures to address pollution, including work on landfill waste, cleaning the Yamuna, dust mitigation, plantation, road infrastructure and waste management."Our government is tackling pollution from a 360-degree perspective to ensure it gradually decreases. We are working on every aspect, be it addressing the mountains of garbage, cleaning the Yamuna, improving road infrastructure, or managing waste, to ensure the people of Delhi enjoy better air quality. Our resolve and policies are absolutely clear, and we are working 24x7 in the public interest," she said.The chief minister also reviewed the progress of waste disposal work with officials and directed them to accelerate the work according to the stipulated timeline.She said the garbage mountains at Bhalswa, Ghazipur and Okhla had caused inconvenience to people travelling through these areas and said the government was continuing efforts to eliminate them.
Article Summary: Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years. She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure.

Article Title: India-US trade talks hit ‘plateau’: Sitharaman says further give-and-take ‘very, very difficult’
Article Text:
Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman

India stresses strategic autonomy in trade negotiations

India-EU pact opens market access

India and US have reached a “plateau” in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement, with further concessions from either side likely to be "very very difficult", finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman said on Monday. Speaking at the Munich Leaders Meeting in New Delhi, she said that while negotiations are still underway, any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side.“The agreement negotiations are still ongoing, although we'd like to believe that both the sides have reached a plateau beyond which giving or taking might be very, very difficult. But maybe if there are rooms to operate from, both sides would do it,” Sitharaman said.She said the agreement was still being “hard and very rigorously negotiated” and that India has a trade surplus with the US. “But what is the predominant feature of the trade relations between India and the US? The trade balance is very much in our favor.”Sitharaman said that the US would naturally want to reduce this trade imbalance and address what it sees as losses built up over the years.She also said that the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.“Negotiation used to be the only platform through which countries could highlight the discrepancies, highlight the lop-sidedness and say, would we want to correct this?” she said.“Tariff was an instrument of negotiation, and tariff had a certain framework within which you will apply it. Today framework is there, tariffs are going,” she said, while stressing that countries still need to negotiate and find “some give and take”.Sitharaman was also asked about maintaining strategic autonomy while negotiating bilateral trade agreements with European countries, including in the context of India procuring Russian oil."There is no Lindsay Graham Bill in Europe...," she said.On the broader question of how bilateral trade agreements can protect a country's interests in an era of multilateralism, Sitharaman said countries were increasingly choosing bilateral partnerships where they saw greater benefit.“Countries choose where multilateralism would benefit them, and there are some unique bilaterals which countries choose to have. The balance is somewhat tilted in favour of the bilateral rather than the multilateral,” she said.She said countries were now increasingly looking for new trade partners and strengthening those relationships through agreements.“Countries are now rapidly catching up with — I would put the EU-India also in a bilateral mode -because it's one in the name of union, but of course within them they have. So, bilaterals today are catching up far more than even initiating or beginning a multilateral. It's not deliberate, but in a way, if you don't do it, you're not moving forward. Countries will have to choose new partners for their trade and strengthen the tie through an agreement. And therefore, newer partnerships are being searched for, and they are tied up bilaterally.”FM Sitharaman cited the India-EU trade agreement as a major example of India's approach to negotiating trade pacts while protecting domestic interests.She said India had opened 92.5 per cent of its tariff lines and around 97 per cent of tariff value under the agreement. The EU, meanwhile, had opened 99 per cent in value terms and possibly 97 per cent of tariff lines.According to Sitharaman, greater access to the European market could support employment in labour-intensive sectors, including footwear, textiles, toys and processed products. Many of these sectors are linked to micro and small enterprises.“Those are all in the micro and small medium industry segment, which are labor-intensive,” Sitharaman said, adding that greater access to the European market could generate “more exports, more jobs”.Sitharaman said bilateral trade agreements were becoming increasingly important as multilateral institutions have weakened.“Multilateralism is not going to go away. But multilateralism has weakened,” she said.She also stressed that multilateralism should continue even as countries increasingly pursue bilateral agreements.“Multilateralism is not going to go away and multilateralism shouldn't go away,” Sitharaman said.The Munich Leaders Meeting, being held in the National Capital, provides a platform for about 100 senior decision-makers and experts to discuss opportunities for stronger cooperation among emerging and middle powers amid profound geopolitical change. Discussions include geoeconomic developments, trade and connectivity, maritime security, defence cooperation and other key international challenges.
Article Summary: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman says India and US have reached a 'plateau' in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement. She said any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side. She also said the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.

Article Title: Jio IPO sees bumper demand: India's largest public issue fully subscribed in just 100 minutes of opening
Article Text:
The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders.

Jio IPO

Jio IPO: Jio Platforms' $3.2 billion initial public offering (IPO) was fully subscribed within less than two hours of bidding opening on Wednesday, as investors rushed to participate in India's biggest-ever share sale. The offering is also the first IPO from billionaire Mukesh Ambani 's Reliance group in two decades.According to a PTI report, the Jio IPO was fully subscribed within 100 minutes of its opening on October 21.The rapid subscription was notable because large IPOs in India often see a slow start, with institutional investors typically placing their bids closer to the closing deadline. By comparison, the National Stock Exchange of India's share sale recently attracted subscriptions for just 42% of the shares on offer on its first day. Hyundai Motor India's IPO had received bids for only 18% of its offering on the opening day.Also Read | Jio IPO, India’s largest public issue, opens for subscription: Price band, GMP to brokerage views - top 10 things to know The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders. The issue will close on Friday, with shares priced in a band of Rs 1,065 to Rs 1,119 apiece.Exchange data showed that institutional investors had bid for 3.25 times the shares reserved for them by Wednesday. Retail participation was lower at that stage, with individual investors applying for 0.22 times their reserved quota.Retail investors have been allocated around one-third of the total offering.The IPO values Jio Platforms at as much as $108.3 billion. Once trading begins on October 28, the company could rank among India's largest listed companies by market capitalisation.Earlier this week, Jio Platforms allotted shares worth $853 million to domestic and international investors, including the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority and BlackRock. The anchor investor portion attracted bids exceeding $25 billion, according to a Reuters report.Backed by global investors such as Meta, Google's parent company Alphabet and other institutional investors, Jio Platforms houses India's largest telecom operator. With more than 500 million subscribers, the business is the world's second-largest telecom operator within a single country, behind China Mobile.This is Reliance's first IPO since 2006. Jio Platforms' telecom business, led by Ambani's son Akash, began operations in 2016. Its strategy was built around the expectation that Indians would use the internet much more extensively if access became almost free. By offering inexpensive data and free voice calls, Jio quickly gained market share from competitors such as Bharti Airtel and Vodafone Idea.
Article Summary: Jio IPO was fully subscribed within 100 minutes of its opening on October 21. The rapid subscription was notable because large IPOs in India often see a slow start. The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders. The issue will close on Friday, with shares priced in a band of Rs 1,065 to Rs1,119 apiece.

Article Title: LPG consumption down, diesel & petrol sales up in September
Article Text:
LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier

NEW DELHI: LPG demand fell by over 9% year-on-year in Sept, while petrol and diesel sales registered growth of 7% and 5%, respectively, provisional data released by the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC) showed.LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier.Month-on-month consumption, however, registered a growth of 8%, up from 2.4 MT.Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT. Petrol and diesel consumption had registered year-on-year growth of 7.9% and 6.5%, respectively, in July.While petrol is largely used as an automobile fuel and its consumption is commensurate with the increasing number of vehicles, diesel is consumed by transport vehicles for passenger and freight movement, besides being used in the agricultural sector.Erratic monsoon conditions due to El Nino boosted demand for diesel for irrigation.Cumulative petrol consumption during Apr-Sept in the current financial year increased 7% to 22.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose 4.8% to 47.9 MT. In contrast, LPG consumption declined 14.9% to 13.8 MT from 16.2 MT during the corresponding period of 2025-26.
Article Summary: LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier. Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT.

Article Title: Bengaluru woman orders curd on Blinkit, finds packet damaged, searches online for customer care number to claim refund, follows WhatsApp link sent by fraudsters and loses Rs 98,000
Article Text:
(AI Image) A homemaker from Vasanth Nagar ordered curd online and received it in a damaged condition





BENGALURU: A 56-year-old homemaker lost Rs 98,000 to cyber fraud after ordering a packet of curd on Blinkit, finding it damaged and searching online for a customer care number to claim a refund.She was allegedly duped after contacting fraudsters posing as customer care representatives and following a link they sent her on WhatsApp.According to a complaint filed by Soundarya (name changed), a resident of an apartment on Palace Cross Road in Vasanth Nagar, she had ordered the curd on October 17. When the packet arrived in a damaged condition, she complained to the delivery agent, who advised her to contact customer care.The woman searched online for a customer care number and called one she found on the internet. The person who answered assured her that a refund would be processed and instructed her to follow certain steps.He then sent her a link on WhatsApp and asked her to upload a photograph of the damaged packet. After she submitted the picture, another person called her, claiming that the refund was being processed and asking her to check her digital payment account.When Soundarya opened the account and entered her password to check the balance, the app suddenly disappeared from the screen. She soon discovered that Rs 98,000 had been debited from her bank account.Realising she had been cheated, she approached the police and sought action. Central Cyber Crime police have registered a case and are investigating the fraud.
Article Summary: A 56-year-old homemaker lost Rs 98,000 to cyber fraud after ordering a packet of curd on Blinkit. She was allegedly duped after contacting fraudsters posing as customer care representatives. Central Cyber Crime police have registered a case and are investigating the fraud.

Article Title: Fireworks, flags and celebrations as student-led movement wins in Serbia; can they deliver reforms?
Article Text:
In Serbia, can a leaderless student movement, with little experience of governing, turn its electoral victory into lasting political change?

From street protests to political power

Can the new government deliver reforms?

Kosovo, Russia and the European Union

Celebrations swept across Serbia after Gen Z-backed candidates defeated president Aleksandar Vucic’s ruling party in a historic election, ending his long grip on power. In Belgrade, crowds filled central squares, cars draped in Serbian flags honked their horns and fireworks lit up the sky as jubilant protesters dismantled barricades around a pro-government encampment near parliament.But beyond the celebrations, a key question remains: Can a leaderless student movement, with little experience of governing, turn its electoral victory into lasting political change?The election follows nearly two years of student-led demonstrations sparked by the collapse of a canopy at the Novi Sad railway station in 2024, which killed 16 people. Protesters blamed corruption and cronyism for the disaster, turning the tragedy into a wider campaign for accountability.Visuals circulating on social media showed crowds taking to the streets of Belgrade and other Serbian cities soon after the election results were announced. The student movement built nationwide support without a single leader and eventually fielded 250 candidates, including academics, lawyers, doctors, farmers, actors and musicians.Its agenda centres on anti-corruption measures, judicial reform and stronger public institutions.The candidates have proposed an independent police unit accountable to prosecutors, transparent appointments to state-owned companies and tighter scrutiny of public infrastructure contracts.However, unity could prove difficult once the movement begins governing.“(The student movement created) such a shift in Serbia's culture; we will just have to see if it lasts,” Katarina Popovic, a professor at the University of Belgrade told news agency Reuters.“We just hope that there are big goals that can keep them together long enough to deconstruct the system,” she added.Under Serbia’s constitution, the student-backed candidates have 90 days to form a government after parliament is convened following the announcement of final election results.The immediate challenges include passing a year-end budget, addressing rising public and private debt, reforming the police and intelligence services, and strengthening the judiciary.The students' victory "is likely to trigger broad institutional and policy changes centred on anti-corruption, the rule of law, and better public services. However, bureaucratic resistance to reforms and the movement’s limited governing experience could make the transition challenging," Teneo Global Research said in a report on Monday.The IMF projects Serbia’s economy to grow 3 per cent in 2026 and 4 per cent in 2027, while inflation rose to 4.1 per cent in September from 2.2 per cent in August. The central bank has held its benchmark interest rate at 5.75 per cent since 2024.“The new government would have to fight its corner,” warned Bozo Prelevic, a Belgrade-based lawyer and former co-minister of the interior, referring to the Serbian Progressive Party (SNS), which is expected to remain a formidable opposition force.The movement has also promised economic changes, including action against retail monopolies to lower food prices, tax relief for lower-income groups, affordable housing initiatives and cheaper medicines.Foreign policy could be another test. The student-backed candidates oppose recognising Kosovo’s independence, declared in 2008, while relations with the European Union remain strained over stalled accession talks and the need to normalise ties with Pristina.The movement has also said it does not intend to impose sanctions on Russia, Serbia’s traditional ally and a major gas supplier. At the same time, the European Commission has offered support for reforms involving the rule of law and media freedom.“I am sure (the Student List) will find a way, just as they have so far, to choose someone capable of governing,” said Savo Manojlovic of the student-friendly Move-Change movement, according to Reuters.
Article Summary: Gen Z-backed candidates defeated president Aleksandar Vucic’s ruling party in a historic election. The election follows nearly two years of student-led demonstrations sparked by the collapse of a canopy at the Novi Sad railway station in 2024. The student movement built nationwide support without a single leader and eventually fielded 250 candidates.

Article Title: Anthropic files for IPO: Losses, dividends & risks to humanity; what investors should know
Article Text:
Anthropic reported $16.3 billion in revenue in the first half of 2026 alongside a net loss of $80.7 billion

Anthropic's 5 year journey

Here are five key takeaways.

Dividends: No payouts in sight

Voting rights: A founder-linked structure

Losses: An $80.7 billion half-year hit

Risks to humanity: The warning in the filing

What the founders get: A potentially historic payday

Anthropic’s planned stock market debut captures a central AI contradiction: surging demand and huge losses, alongside warnings that its technology could threaten humanity. The Claude maker plans to list on Nasdaq as ANT, but has yet to set the number of shares or their price range. The filing offers a closer look at what investors would be buying.Founded in 2021 by former OpenAI employees, Anthropic reported $16.3 billion in revenue in the first half of 2026 alongside a net loss of $80.7 billion. Revenue growth has been rapid, largely driven by business customers using Claude and related AI software. It expects losses to continue as it invests in computing, research, safety and expansion. Remaining competitive, it says, depends on advanced models, specialist staff and capital.The disclosures go beyond finances. They confirm there are no near-term dividends, describe a share structure that gives a founder-linked vehicle decisive voting power, and detail risks ranging from regulatory scrutiny to advanced AI moving beyond human control.Anthropic has never declared or paid cash dividends and does not expect to do so in the foreseeable future. It plans to retain available funds and future earnings for operations and expansion.Any dividend would be at the board’s discretion, based on its financial condition and capital needs. Its credit agreement also limits payouts, even if no money is outstanding under the facility.Anthropic has four authorised classes of common stock, with Class A and Class N as series of Participating Common Stock. Their voting rights differ. Class A shareholders get one vote per share on general matters. Class N generally carries no voting rights; Class T, issued to the LTBT, votes only on specified matters. Class E, intended for employees other than co-founders, also lacks general voting rights, subject to protections.Class F, to be issued to Founder LLC, carries votes equal to 50.1% of total voting power on general shareholder matters, including elections of directors other than Class T directors. Votes will be cast under the Founder LLC agreement, potentially limiting ordinary shareholders’ influence after listing.Anthropic’s net loss rose from $1.5 billion in 2023 to $8.3 billion in 2024 and $42 billion in 2025. In the six months to 30 June 2026, it lost $80.7 billion, compared with nearly $13 billion a year earlier.The figure needs context: $72.4 billion of the first-half loss came from changes in the fair value of convertible promissory notes, derivative liabilities and SAFEs, primarily as the value of outstanding notes rose alongside Anthropic’s valuation. The net loss is not a simple measure of cash spent on operations. Even so, the company says it is highly capital-intensive, expects costs and losses to continue, and may never achieve or sustain profitability.The filing says advanced AI systems could “pose catastrophic or existential risks to humanity” without safeguards, oversight and security. Misuse, replication, weaponisation or substantial autonomy could heighten those dangers. Even isolated or simulated harmful behaviour, it says, could trigger public concern, regulatory scrutiny, litigation and reputational damage, regardless of actual harm.Anthropic also describes “closing the loop”: using successive models to design, train, test and optimise the next generation. But flaws or biases could spread into later systems and become harder to detect or fix. AI research could outpace the ability to evaluate and safeguard new models, a concern alongside chief executive Dario Amodei’s calls for more cautious development. The company warns that the danger could grow as AI systems automate more of the research and development process itself.The offering could sharply increase the paper wealth of Anthropic’s seven founders, including chief executive Dario Amodei and his sister, co-founder Daniela. Reports say the founders collectively hold nearly 500 million shares, but their post-IPO ownership and any planned sales are unclear.The final valuation, offer price and size of the sale remain undecided, making any windfall uncertain. But Class F stock could preserve substantial founder-linked control as public investors buy in.
Article Summary: Claude maker plans to list on Nasdaq as ANT, but has yet to set the number of shares or their price range. Anthropic reported $16.3 billion in revenue in the first half of 2026 alongside a net loss of $80.7 billion. It expects losses to continue as it invests in computing, research and safety.

Article Title: AI giant Anthropic to make Wall Street debut next month; could be biggest ever initial public sale of stock: Key details from Claude maker's filing
Article Text:
Anthropic has proposed a dual-class share structure

Who will lead the IPO, and how will shares be structured

A public-benefit company with an AI safety mission

Revenue growth, legal costs and the wider AI market

Anthropic, the artificial intelligence company behind Claude, has filed for an initial public offering (IPO) in the US, taking a major step towards what could become one of the biggest stock market listings in history.The company said it had submitted a registration statement to the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) for a proposed offering of its Class A common stock.Anthropic plans to list its shares on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker symbol “ANT”. The company has not yet determined the number of shares it will offer or the price range for the IPO. The proposed listing, which could take place as early as next month, will test investor appetite for artificial intelligence companies amid growing scrutiny of the sector's spending, profitability and long-term growth prospects.Valued at $965 billion after its May 2026 funding round, Anthropic has emerged as one of the biggest players in the global AI industry.Anthropic has appointed a group of major investment banks to underwrite the proposed offering. Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, JPMorgan Securities and Citigroup are among the underwriters, alongside RBC Capital Markets, UBS Securities, BMO Capital Markets and BNP Paribas.The filing outlines a share structure that distinguishes between voting and non-voting stock.Each share of Class A common stock will carry one vote, while Class N common stock will have no voting rights. The company said its Class N shareholders are primarily strategic business partners.Anthropic also plans to issue a single share of Class F common stock to a limited liability company established by its co-founders, known as Founder LLC. The filing further states that the Class A common stock will not be convertible.Chief executive Dario Amodei holds 240.6 million Class A shares before the offering, with the total rising to 245.3 million when shares subject to voting proxies are included.The company has also contributed 846,840,960 shares of Class N common stock to Anthropic Public Benefit Fund LLC, reflecting its public-benefit structure.Anthropic operates as a public benefit corporation, the statement said with a legal structure that requires its management to balance financial performance with broader public interests. The company said it intends to direct a meaningful portion of its resources towards ensuring that frontier AI is safe and that its benefits are widely distributed.The structure sets Anthropic apart from a conventional profit-focused company, particularly as it prepares to answer to public-market investors. Its commitment to AI safety will be closely watched alongside its commercial performance, given wider concerns about the risks posed by increasingly capable AI systems.Anthropic also said it does not expect to pay dividends in the foreseeable future, signalling that it intends to retain resources for its business and future investments.Anthropic's filing comes as investors weigh the company's rapid expansion against the substantial costs and risks associated with developing advanced AI systems.The company recorded a $1.5 billion charge in the three months ended September 30, 2025, to settle the Bartz litigation, a copyright dispute brought by authors who alleged that their books had been used without permission to train Claude. The settlement highlights the legal liabilities that can accompany the development of generative AI models.The IPO is also expected to provide a clearer picture of the economics underpinning the AI boom. Anthropic and rival OpenAI sit at the centre of a network of chipmakers, cloud providers, data-centre operators and other businesses that have invested heavily in anticipation of sustained demand for AI services.
